Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Holdings Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Holdings' Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong financial results relative to our guidance, significant progress in grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, a disciplined dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, and a robust rate base growth outlook underpinned by key strategic assumptions.

These elements reflect the resilience of our diversified generation portfolio, our focus on reliable renewables, and our ability to capitalize on load growth from hyperscale data centers and electrification trends while managing costs effectively. Let me touch briefly on each before turning it over to Michael for the deeper financial dive.

On the financial front, we saw beats across key metrics thanks to favorable power prices, hedging success, and renewable contributions. Our grid modernization efforts are enhancing reliability and unlocking new revenues through advanced tech like AMI and ADMS. Our dividend approach continues to deliver growing yields with sustainable payouts, and our rate base expansion positions us for EPS growth amid regulatory and policy tailwinds.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss the financials in detail.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. For the second quarter of 2024, we reported adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.72 and consolidated revenues of $4.28 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.6 billion, primarily focused on renewables development, grid hardening, and transmission upgrades. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

Let me kick off our prepared remarks with an overview of our financial performance relative to the guidance we provided back in April. Overall, we delivered a strong beat across our core metrics, reflecting the resilience of our diversified generation portfolio, robust load growth from hyperscale data centers, and effective execution on our hedging and capital deployment strategies.

Starting with the top line, we reported consolidated revenues of $4.28 billion for the quarter, surpassing the midpoint of our guidance range of $4.0 to $4.1 billion by approximately 5%. This outperformance was driven primarily by our unregulated merchant segment, where power prices realized 12% above our forward curve assumptions, bolstered by elevated summer demand in key ISO markets like PJM and ERCOT. Regulated utility revenues came in at $2.45 billion, right at the top end of our $2.4 to $2.45 billion guide, thanks to authorized ROE recovery in our Midwest and Southeast footprints, including constructive outcomes from our recent Virginia rate case settlement with the SCC, which added $85 million to annual revenues on a prospective basis.

Adjusted EBITDA landed at $1.12 billion, exceeding our guidance of $1.0 to $1.05 billion by 8%. Margins expanded to 26.2% from 24.8% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting lower-than-expected natural gas fuel costs—our Henry Hub hedges locked in at an average of $2.85 per MMBtu, 15% below spot—and higher contributions from our renewables fleet, which operated at a 95% capacity factor amid favorable wind resource in the Plains. We also benefited from $45 million in production tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act, accelerating our clean energy transition.

On the bottom line, adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.72, handily beating our $1.50 to $1.60 guidance range by 11% at the midpoint. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of EPS growth year-over-year, up 9% from $1.58 in Q2 2023. GAAP EPS was $1.55, after adjusting for $120 million in non-recurring items, including mark-to-market losses on our nuclear decommissioning trusts and one-time O&M charges from unscheduled outages at our legacy coal fleet in Appalachia.

Segment-wise, our Regulated Utilities segment, which represents 55% of our EBITDA, delivered $680 million, 4% above guidance, fueled by 2.2% weather-normalized load growth—led by residential electrification and C&I demand from manufacturing reshoring in the Carolinas. Merchant Generation, our highest-margin business at 35% EBITDA contribution, generated $520 million, smashing expectations by 15% on the back of strong capacity auction clears in PJM's BRA—where we secured $140/kW-year for our 2.5 GW combined-cycle fleet—and elevated real-time energy prices in ERCOT during the July heat dome, averaging $85/MWh.

Renewables and Storage rounded out at $250 million, 10% ahead of guide, with our 1.8 GW wind portfolio in Oklahoma and Texas achieving P50-plus production, and our first 200 MW/400 MWh BESS project in California dispatching 85% utilization into the CAISO evening ramp. This segment's growth underscores our strategic pivot: we've now locked in 3.2 GW of new PPAs with tech majors like Google and Microsoft, at weighted-average pricing 20% above market, supporting our goal of 50% carbon-free generation by 2030.

Regionally, performance was solid across the board. In the Northeast PJM zone, where we have 40% of our capacity, cooler-than-normal weather tempered cooling loads by 3%, but this was more than offset by 5% data center load growth and our fleet's 92% availability. Texas ERCOT shone brightest, with merchant margins up 25% YoY on scarcity pricing—our gas plants ran flat-out, capturing $200 million in uplift. Southeast regulated ops were steady, though we saw some pressure from milder hydro conditions in Georgia, partially mitigated by our $300 million grid hardening capex under FERC Order 881.

Key headwinds we called out—higher O&M from inflationary pressures on turbine maintenance and supply chain delays for solar panels—totaled $60 million, in line with our sensitivities. But these were dwarfed by tailwinds: our natural gas hedging program covered 85% of Q3 needs at $3.10/MMBtu, shielding us from the recent Waha basis blowout, and AFUDC equity of $35 million from our $2.5 billion construction pipeline, including the 800 MW offshore wind lease off Virginia Beach.

Strategically, this quarter validates our 'Reliable Renewables' framework. We're accelerating SMR deployment with our TerraPower JV—FEED studies complete for a 345 MW unit online by 2028—and our 1 GW battery pipeline positions us to monetize ERCOT's ancillary services market, projected to grow 15% CAGR through 2030 per EIA forecasts. Compared to peers like NextEra and Dominion, our 12% FCF yield remains top-quartile, with leverage at 3.4x net debt-to-EBITDA, giving us ample dry powder for bolt-ons amid the M&A wave in batteryless assets.

In summary on this overview, we not only met but exceeded our Q2 guidance, delivering shareholder value through disciplined ops and forward-thinking capex. For the full year, we're raising the midpoint of our Adjusted EPS guidance to $6.55-$6.75 from $6.40-$6.65, incorporating $150 million in incremental renewables PTCs and sustained load growth.

Before moving on, I want to spend a few minutes on one of our highest-conviction growth drivers: grid modernization and smart grid initiatives. As we navigate the accelerating electrification megatrend—fueled by EV adoption, data center hyperscalers, and industrial onshoring—our investments here are delivering outsized returns, both operationally and financially. We've deployed over $1.2 billion in capital expenditures since 2022 across our 15-state footprint, with a forward-looking $850 million allocated for 2025, representing about 18% of our total CapEx budget. This isn't just table stakes; it's a strategic differentiator positioning Apex Power Holdings for 8-10% annual rate base growth through the decade.

First, on advanced metering infrastructure and customer-facing digitalization: We've now reached 92% AMI penetration across our 4.2 million customer accounts, up from 75% at the end of 2023. This includes the rollout of next-gen solid-state meters from Itron and Landis+Gyr, integrated with our Oracle Utilities Meter Data Management System. The impact? Real-time interval data is enabling dynamic pricing programs that have boosted our demand response participation by 35% YoY, clipping peak demand by 450 MW during last summer's heatwaves—equivalent to shaving $22 million off our capacity procurement costs. On the residential side, our myApex app, powered by AMI data, has seen a 28% increase in customer engagement, driving voluntary time-of-use shifts that reduced system lambda by 12% during evenings. Financially, this is accretive: AMI-related O&M savings hit $45 million in the first nine months, with a three-year payback on our $320 million investment.

Second, the heart of our smart grid: advanced distribution management systems and distributed energy resource management systems. We've fully implemented GE Vernova's GridOS ADMS across our Midwest and Southeast operating companies, covering 85% of our 150,000 miles of distribution lines. This platform orchestrates volt/VAR optimization, fault location isolation and service restoration, and integrated outage management. Results speak for themselves: our SAIDI improved 22% YoY to 78 minutes, and SAIFI dropped 18% to 0.92 interruptions per customer—putting us in the top quartile of EEI index peers like Duke Energy and Southern Company. In Q3 alone—extrapolating forward—FLISR events prevented 1.2 million customer-minutes of outage, translating to $18 million in avoided restoration costs and regulatory credits under our multi-year rate plans.

On DERMS, with renewables now at 28% of our generation mix, up from 22% last year, we're managing 2.5 GW of rooftop solar, battery storage, and behind-the-meter resources via Siemens' Spectrum Power DERMS. This has unlocked $65 million in ancillary services revenue from MISO and PJM markets, including frequency regulation and ramping services. A prime example: our 200 MW BESS fleet in ERCOT, co-optimized with DERMS, captured $12 million in scarcity pricing during the August polar vortex event—delivering 15% IRR on that asset class.

Regionally, this plays out differently, reflecting local market dynamics. In the Northeast PJM territory, 40% of our load, we're prioritizing resiliency against extreme weather, with $250 million invested in microgrid tie-ins and hardened substations. We've deferred $180 million in traditional T&D CapEx by deploying 150 MW of grid-edge storage and demand flexibility. Texas ERCOT, 15% of our footprint, focuses on scale and volatility: our smart inverter standards, compliant with ERCOT's new DER handbook, have integrated 800 MW of customer-sited solar without grid stability issues, even as wholesale prices spiked to $5,000/MWh last winter. Out West in CAISO and WECC, amid wildfire risks, we've deployed 5,000 PMUs for wide-area monitoring, reducing T&D losses by 7.2% to 4.8% system-wide—ahead of FERC Order 881 mandates.

The trends shaping our strategy include electrification: EV load growing 22% YoY, data centers adding a 1.2 GW pipeline by 2027 in Virginia and Ohio. The Inflation Reduction Act's $370 billion in incentives, including ITC extensions, de-risk our $2.5 billion five-year plan—90% qualifying for 30-50% tax credits. Cyber threats are addressed with Dragos and Nozomi OT security stacks, achieving zero material incidents.

We're partnering with ABB for SF6-free switchgear and Schneider Electric for EcoStruxure Grid, plus a JV with NextEra on HVDC lines for the $100 billion queue backlog. Monetization includes rate base recovery at 9.5-10.5% ROE and piloting transactive energy markets for $50 million new revenues by 2026.

Bottom line: These initiatives drove $112 million in incremental EBITDA in the first nine months, with a blended IRR of 14%. We expect 25-30 basis points EPS accretion in 2025.

As we wrap up our financial review, I'd like to dive into our dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, which remains a cornerstone of our capital allocation framework. In the Utilities sector, where regulated cash flows from our rate base assets provide predictable earnings, we've built a reputation for delivering reliable, growing dividends—much like our peers at NextEra Energy and Duke Energy. Our policy underscores our commitment to total shareholder return, balancing attractive yields with reinvestment for our clean energy transition.

Today, our Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.62 per share, marking a 4% increase year-over-year and our 28th consecutive annual hike. This brings our annualized dividend to $2.48 per share, yielding approximately 4.2% at current share prices—positioned competitively within the S&P 500 Utilities Index, where the sector average hovers around 3.8%. Over the past five years, we've grown our dividend at a compound annual growth rate of 5.2%, outpacing inflation and supported by our regulated ROE of 10.25% in key jurisdictions.

Turning to our payout ratio strategy, defined as dividends paid as a percentage of adjusted funds from operations, or AFFO—a metric favored by rating agencies like S&P and Moody's—for the trailing 12 months, our payout ratio stands at 72%, within our long-term target range of 65% to 75%. This aligns with sector leaders: Southern Company's at 71%, Dominion Energy's at 68%, and Exelon's at 74%. We've trended downward from 78% in 2020, reflecting AFFO growth from our $2.8 billion rate base expansion and efficiencies.

This range fits our portfolio—65% regulated thermal and hydro, 25% renewables like our 1.2 GW solar fleet and 800 MW wind assets, 10% nuclear—generating resilient FCF even with nat gas at $2.75/MMBtu in Q2 vs. $3.20 last year. We leave headroom for $1.6 billion capex, 70% into grid hardening and renewables under IRA ITC/PTC.

Regionally, Southeast SERC/MRO sees 8% YoY demand lift from data centers, sub-70% payout; ERCOT offsets renewables risks with batteries, 68% ratio; CAISO at 74% with LCFS credits.

We've implemented AI-driven AFFO modeling for 1.6-1.8x coverage 3-5 years out, incorporating power curves and $3.2 billion capex for CCUS and SMRs. Amid 4.8% debt costs, we maintain A- rating.

We guide 4-6% dividend growth through the decade, payout flexing 65-75%, de-risking transition with 10%+ EPS CAGR.

Finally, as we discuss capex execution, let's dive deeper into our rate base growth outlook and key assumptions. Rate base is the cornerstone of our regulated earnings, and we're reaffirming our multi-year trajectory amid load growth, IRA extensions, and FERC Order 1920.

As of June 30, 2024, our consolidated rate base is $28.4 billion, up 5.8% YoY from $26.8 billion, reflecting $1.2 billion in-service like Windridge Wind Farm and Texas solar-storage. We've delivered 5.2% CAGR 2020-2023, beating peers.

We guide 6.0% to 6.5% annual growth through 2028, to $37.5-$38.5 billion—a 6.2% five-year CAGR. Post-2028, 5.5-6.0%, from $15.2 billion capex plan, 85% queued.

Drivers: 1. Generation (45%): 2.3 GW renewables/storage by 2027, like 800 MW Lone Star Solar + BESS, coal retirements backfilled. 2. T&D (35%): $4.8 billion hardening, CREZ II, FERC 1920 lines. 3. Customer/tech (20%): 95% AMI, $450 million EV infra.

Key assumptions: timely rate cases, 10.0-10.5% ROE; 2.1% load CAGR + data centers; $3.0-3.1B annual capex, 3% inflation; IRA tailwinds.

Risks mitigated, supports 7-8% EPS CAGR, balancing 70% carbon-free by 2030 with returns.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Michael. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Tami Zakaria with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Tami Zakaria: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for grid modernization and smart grid initiatives?

John Reynolds: Certainly, Tami. As Michael outlined in detail, our grid mod investments are a top priority, with over $1.2 billion deployed since 2022 driving reliability gains like 22% better SAIDI and new ancillary revenues. We're focused on AMI at 92%, ADMS coverage, and DERMS for our growing renewables mix, positioning us ahead on electrification and resilience.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Russo with UBS. Please go ahead.

Brian Russo: What is your outlook for dividend growth and payout ratio?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Brian. We're committed to 4-6% annual growth through the decade, supported by our 72% TTM AFFO payout within the 65-75% target. This balances reinvestment in our rate base and renewables while delivering a competitive 4.2% yield, with coverage strengthening to 1.6-1.8x via AI forecasting and IRA benefits.

Operator: Our next question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith: How are you mitigating risks related to rate base growth assumptions amid regulatory and load uncertainties?

Lisa Patel: Great question, Julien. Our 6-6.5% growth guide embeds conservative assumptions like 2.1% load CAGR plus data center upside, timely rate cases, and capex execution with hedged inflation. We stress-test for downside—higher rates or lower load—and still hit 5.5%, while multi-year plans and IRA de-risk the queue. CWIP and formula rates in key states provide buffers.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q2 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
